think_procedure: Let me analyze the wal_buffers knob step by step: 1) wal_buffers controls the amount of shared memory used for WAL data that has not yet been written to disk. 2) It accepts integer values representing the number of disk-page-sized buffers. 3) The key special behavior is when wal_buffers is set to -1, which enables automatic sizing where PostgreSQL automatically chooses an appropriate value based on shared_buffers (typically 1/32 of shared_buffers, with minimum and maximum limits). 4) When set to -1, the system calculates the optimal buffer size automatically rather than using a fixed user-specified value. 5) This automatic behavior is fundamentally different from specifying an explicit number of buffers, making -1 a special value that breaks the natural numerical ordering.
